comparison: Strong agreement on ATUM-Tomo methodological development (C6, C28-C46, C59-C62). Both evaluations find the method well-supported with detailed characterization. OpenEval emphasizes technical parameters and artifact documentation (C66-C67, C73-C74), while peer review highlights transparency and compatibility findings. Peer review includes C63 (future applications) which OpenEval evaluates separately as uncertain.

Strong agreement on BBB leakage cellular and ultrastructural findings (C7, C16-C27, C47-C50, C70, C72, C76-C77). Both evaluations find converging evidence from multiple imaging modalities compelling. OpenEval emphasizes multi-modal validation and resolution advantages, while peer review praises the CLEM approach and proof-of-principle demonstration. OpenEval includes additional tracer characterization claims (C64-C65) and methodological details (C39) not grouped in peer review R3.

Strong agreement on ATUM-SEM and ET background/limitations (C1-C3, C8-C14). Both evaluations accept these as established technical context. OpenEval focuses on C1-C3, C8-C12 for ATUM-SEM, while peer review groups all background claims together (C1-C14 including ET limitations C4-C5, C13-C14). Both note these provide rationale for ATUM-Tomo development.

Strong agreement on BBB biological interpretations and transcytosis mechanism (C51-C58, C75). Both evaluations support the vesicular transport interpretation. OpenEval includes direct observational evidence (C48-C49, C70) and notes mechanism remains somewhat inferential, while peer review accepts biological interpretations without critique and suggests expanding scientific context discussion. OpenEval emphasizes glycocalyx correlation (C55, C70).

Agreement on ET technology background (C4-C5, C13-C14). OpenEval evaluates these as supported established ET limitations with appropriate citations, providing rationale for ATUM-Tomo. Peer review groups these with broader technical background (C1-C14) and accepts without challenge as established context.

Partial overlap on technical parameters. OpenEval evaluates BBB ultrastructure background (C15) and ET acquisition parameters (C68-C69) as supporting reproducibility. Peer review R5 includes these claims (C68-C69, C15 via C71 context) within broader affirmation of methodological detail sufficiency for replication, also covering additional claims (C39, C64-C67, C71, C73-C74).

Minimal overlap on C15 (BBB ultrastructure background). OpenEval groups C15 with technical ET parameters as standard documentation. Peer review R4 includes C15 with biological interpretations and BBB context, accepting without critique but suggesting expanded discussion of scientific context.

Disagreement on future applications claim (C63). OpenEval evaluates this as UNCERTAIN, noting the claim about 'diverse biological research areas' is speculative and not directly tested beyond the single biological system. Peer review R1 includes C63 with supported methodological development claims, implicitly accepting the broader applicability statement.

Partial overlap on methodological detail claims (C66-C67, C73-C74). OpenEval includes these with core ATUM-Tomo development as documenting limitations and artifacts. Peer review R5 groups these with broader methodological detail affirmation (C39, C64-C69, C71, C73-C74), praising sufficiency for replication and adoptability.

Minimal overlap on experimental workflow and tracer details (C39, C64-C65). OpenEval includes these with BBB ultrastructural evidence as supporting multi-modal validation. Peer review R5 groups these with broader methodological detail documentation, affirming sufficiency for replication.

Minimal overlap on observational evidence (C48-C49, C70). OpenEval groups these with transcytosis mechanism interpretation (C51-C58, C75), noting direct evidence of intact tight junctions with intracellular nanoparticles. Peer review R3 includes these claims within broader proof-of-principle CLEM demonstration (C7, C16-C27, C47-C50, C70, C72, C76-C77).

Minimal overlap on C71 only. OpenEval does not explicitly evaluate C71 in isolation but includes it contextually with transcytosis mechanism. Peer review R5 includes C71 with broader methodological detail affirmation.
